newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says no inflationary pressures.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says no inflationary pressures.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Thursday Canada had no inflationary pressures at the moment, and he said he had no difference of opinion with Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen on the issue.
"The fight against inflation is never won. You've always got to watch it," he told reporters, adding however: "There are no inflationary pressures in Canada at the present time."
Asked if he and Thiessen viewed the risks of inflation differently, he said: "There are no differences of opinion with Mr. Thiessen and myself.
"I made it very clear that we paid a very, very strong penalty to get inflation down, and we're going to keep inflation down. We're not going to give up the benefits of being a low-inflation nation."
A reporter asked whether Thiessen, given the lack of inflationary pressures, should cut interest rates further. Martin replied: "Mr. Thiessen does his job very, very well."
The Canadian Broadcasting Corp reported that Martin said Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan agrees with him that inflation is not a threat anymore.
